generated_examples.rule: Each source becomes one research-only example. No parcel contamination determination, landfill surrender, mine-entry location, ground-stability conclusion, radon measurement or Future Growth score is inferred.

second_pass_examples.rule: Recheck Part 2A determination, planning condition, environmental permit, definite closure/surrender, mining permission and remediation/verification as separate legal/process states.

third_pass_examples.rule: Recheck dataset update cycles, terminated designations, historic records, permit status, monitoring/aftercare and current authority evidence. No-data and old-data states remain explicit.

fourth_pass_examples.rule: Recheck national/map/model evidence against exact parcel geometry, conceptual site model, intrusive investigation, engineering assessment, gas/radon measurement and verification. Susceptibility or proximity alone is never promoted.

extra_examples.fact: The national Planning Data contaminated-land dataset currently has zero records and no provider collection.
extra_examples.gate: Zero platform records must not become 'no contaminated land'; use the LPA/EA exact-site evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Part 2A uses a specific legal test for contaminated land and remediation.
extra_examples.gate: Detected contaminants or historic use are not equivalent to a statutory determination.

extra_examples.fact: A significant pollutant linkage requires a contaminant, pathway and receptor.
extra_examples.gate: A source alone cannot be scored as an unacceptable complete linkage.

extra_examples.fact: LCRM starts with desk study/site walkover but can require intrusive investigation and quantitative assessment.
extra_examples.gate: Historic map or database screening does not replace intrusive evidence where required.

extra_examples.fact: Stage 2 selects feasible remediation options against relevant contaminant linkages.
extra_examples.gate: Selected option is not evidence that remediation occurred or met objectives.

extra_examples.fact: Stage 3 requires remediation followed by verification and, where needed, long-term monitoring.
extra_examples.gate: Works completion without verification must not be promoted to 'clean/remediated'.

extra_examples.fact: A local Part 2A register records specified statutory actions after determination/remediation steps.
extra_examples.gate: No register entry cannot be interpreted as no contamination or no planning remediation history.

extra_examples.fact: The Special Sites dataset includes current and terminated designations.
extra_examples.gate: A historical Special Site record must be checked for current designation status before use.

extra_examples.fact: Environment Agency warns historic landfill data may be incomplete, especially for pre-licensing sites.
extra_examples.gate: No polygon hit is not proof no waste was historically deposited.

extra_examples.fact: Historic landfill means no environmental permit is currently in force for the landfill record.
extra_examples.gate: Historic-landfill status does not itself establish a Part 2A contaminated-land determination.

extra_examples.ref: Closed permitted landfill versus surrendered permit
extra_examples.fact: EPR landfill data includes operational and closed permitted sites.
extra_examples.gate: Closed status must not be collapsed into environmental-permit surrender.

extra_examples.ref: Stopped accepting waste versus definite closure
extra_examples.fact: Environment Agency written agreement is required for definite closure under the landfill process.
extra_examples.gate: Operational cessation alone is not definite closure.

extra_examples.fact: Aftercare continues between definite closure and accepted permit surrender for relevant landfills.
extra_examples.gate: A closed landfill may remain regulated for years or decades; do not score it as unrestricted land.

extra_examples.fact: Environment Agency will not accept surrender while active control measures remain necessary.
extra_examples.gate: Pumping, gas extraction or other active controls indicate surrender-readiness has not been demonstrated.

extra_examples.ref: Planning approval on landfill versus pollution acceptability
extra_examples.fact: Landfill surrender guidance separately considers pollution risk even where planning authority has approved development.
extra_examples.gate: Planning approval does not prove environmental-permit surrender criteria are met.

extra_examples.ref: Inert landfill versus zero settlement risk
extra_examples.fact: Inert landfills may still require topographic surveys and stability evidence during aftercare.
extra_examples.gate: Inert waste must not be treated as geotechnically risk-free.

extra_examples.ref: Coal high-risk area versus mine-entry location
extra_examples.fact: Development High Risk Area mapping determines when a CMRA is commonly required.
extra_examples.gate: Area classification does not locate an exact mine entry or prove one intersects the parcel.

extra_examples.fact: Mine-entry positions may require intrusive investigation when layout or quantum depends on them.
extra_examples.gate: A desktop CMRA must not be treated as exact shaft-location verification where intrusive work is needed.

extra_examples.fact: Mining Remediation Authority advice supports planning but developer responsibility for safe and stable development remains.
extra_examples.gate: Advice received is not a warranty of ground stability.

extra_examples.fact: Authority policy generally seeks to avoid building over or close to mine entries even where treatment exists.
extra_examples.gate: Capping/treatment records alone must not be scored as unrestricted buildability.

extra_examples.fact: Mine-gas assessment is prudent where source, pathway and occupied receptor can exist.
extra_examples.gate: Coalfield location alone is not a measured gas concentration, but absence of known workings is not zero risk.

extra_examples.ref: Coal map viewer versus detailed search
extra_examples.fact: The free viewer exposes selected national coal-mining information.
extra_examples.gate: Map-viewer screening is not a detailed property/mineral search or site investigation.

extra_examples.ref: Historical mine plan versus current physical condition
extra_examples.fact: Current access services expose historic plans, deeds, licences and geological records.
extra_examples.gate: Archive evidence does not prove present treatment condition, void stability or gas regime.

extra_examples.fact: Mining Remediation Authority issues mining-related licences and agreements.
extra_examples.gate: Mining permission must remain separate from planning, environmental permitting and remediation verification.

extra_examples.fact: GeoSure identifies potential natural ground hazards using mapped geological susceptibility.
extra_examples.gate: Susceptibility category is not a site-specific probability of foundation failure.

extra_examples.fact: Open GeoSure is generalised to roughly 65 km² hexagonal cells.
extra_examples.gate: Do not transfer one cell's class directly to an exact parcel, borehole or foundation design.

extra_examples.fact: Shrink-swell susceptibility reflects geological conditions that can contribute to ground movement.
extra_examples.gate: Foundation solution still requires exact soil, moisture, vegetation and loading evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Soluble-rock susceptibility indicates where dissolution-related instability may occur.
extra_examples.gate: Mapped susceptibility does not prove a cavity or sinkhole exists under the target footprint.

extra_examples.fact: BGS maps potential collapsible deposits at 1:50,000.
extra_examples.gate: Potential must not be converted into observed collapse or a quantified settlement without investigation.

extra_examples.fact: Soft deposits can compress under loads or groundwater changes.
extra_examples.gate: Mapped susceptibility does not quantify settlement for the proposed structure and loading pattern.

extra_examples.fact: BGS states GeoSure landslide susceptibility does not determine temporal distribution of landsliding.
extra_examples.gate: High susceptibility is not proof an active landslide is occurring today.

extra_examples.ref: No landslide event point versus no slope risk
extra_examples.fact: NLD points reference reported landslide events rather than complete mapped susceptibility.
extra_examples.gate: No event point is not a clean absence test for slope instability.

extra_examples.ref: Running sand susceptibility versus excavation outcome
extra_examples.fact: Running sand can depend on groundwater conditions, excavation and local material behaviour.
extra_examples.gate: Map potential is not proof a proposed excavation will encounter flowing ground.

extra_examples.ref: Radon Affected Area versus measured indoor level
extra_examples.fact: UKradon separates area checking from measurement of yearly average building radon.
extra_examples.gate: Affected-area status is not a building measurement.

extra_examples.ref: Indicative radon map versus definitive address search
extra_examples.fact: UKradon distinguishes indicative 1 km/postcode information from definitive address searches.
extra_examples.gate: Use exact address/building evidence rather than a regional maximum band when assessing a property.

extra_examples.ref: Exact canonical parcel ground-risk stack gate
extra_examples.fact: Contamination, landfill, mining, natural ground hazards and radon each require different evidence and can coexist on one development parcel.
extra_examples.gate: No promotion until exact canonical parcel geometry is reconciled with current LPA/EA/MRA/BGS/UKHSA evidence plus required site investigation and verification states.
